title: खोटाङ जिल्ला दिक्तेल रूपाकोट मझुवागढी नगरपालिका वडा नं. ३, बाम्राङको समुदायमा रहेका जातजातीमा खानेपानीको अवस्था
nepali: पानी यस पृथ्वीमा रहेका सजिव वस्तुका लागि अति महत्वपूर्ण वस्तु हो । त्यस मध्ये पृथ्वीको सर्वश्रेष्ठ प्राणीमा मानव जाती पर्दछ । त्यसैले मानव जातीका लागि खानेपानी अति नै महत्वपूर्ण मानिन्छ ताकि उपयुक्त खानेपानीको अभावमा मानिसको वृद्घी विकासमा समेत अवरोध हुने भएका कारण नेपालका विभिन्न भेगमा खानेपानीको पर्याप्तताको अवस्था कस्तो छ भनि सम्पूर्ण भुगोलको प्रतिनिधित्व हुनेगरी खोटाङ जिल्लाको दिक्तेल रुपाकोट मझुवागढी नगरपालीका वडा नं. ३, बाम्राङको खानेपानीको अवस्था सम्बन्धि अध्ययन गरिएको हो । यो अनुसन्धानात्मक लेख खोटाङ जिल्ला दिक्तेल रुपाकोट मझुवागढी नगरपालिका वडा नं. ३, बाम्राङका समूदायमा परिमाणत्मक तथा गुणात्मक अनुसन्धान विधि अन्र्तगत सम्भाव्य नमूना छनौट विधि मध्ये चिठ्ठा विधिको प्रयोग गरी जम्मा १२० घर नमूनाको लागि छनौट गरीयो । त्यसमध्ये ब्राह्मण ८ घर, क्षेत्री २६ घर, जनजाती ७० घर र दलित १४ घर छनौट गरी आवश्यक प्रश्नावली भराई तथ्याङ्क सङ्कलन गर्दै प्राथमिक श्रोतबाट तथ्याङ्क सङ्कलनका साथ आवश्यक अन्य तथ्याङ्कको लागि द्वित्तीय श्रोत समेतको प्रयोग गरी अनुसन्धानलाई १२० घर परिवारका सदस्यहरुबाट जम्मा १२० जनालाई नमूनाको रुपमा लिई २०७८ साल फाल्गुण महिनामा गरिएको एक सर्वेक्षण बाट ५१.६७ प्रतिशत घर परिवारले धाराको, ४३.३३ प्रतिशत घर परिवारले पाइपको, ३.३३ प्रतिशत घरपरिवारले कुवाको तथा १.६७ प्रतिशत घर परिवारले खोलाको खानेपानी प्रयोग गर्ने गरेको र सबै भन्दा बढिदलित समूदायमा ७१.४२ प्रतिशतले पाइपको माध्यमबाट खानेपानी प्रयोग गर्ने गरेको पाइएको छ भने सबैभन्दा कम ब्राह्मण समूदायमा २० प्रतिशतमा मात्र पाइपको पहँुच भएको पाइएको छ । समग्रमा ३३.३३प्रतिशत घर परिवारमा मात्र घरैमा पानीको पहुँच छ । ब्राह्मण र जनजाती समूदायमा सबैभन्दा बढि४०÷४० प्रतिशत र सबैभन्दा कम दलित समूदायमा १४.२८ प्रतिशत रहेको छ । एक घर एक धाराकोपहुुँच ३१.६७ प्रतिशत घर परिवारमा देखिन्छ भने सबैभन्दा बढि ब्राह्मण समूदायमा ८० प्रतिशत घरधुरीमाधारा रहेको छ भने सबैभन्दा कम दलित समूदायमा १४.२८ प्रतिशत घरधुरीमा धारा रहेको छ ।खानेपानीको पर्याप्ततालाई हेर्दा ८५ प्रतिशत घरधुरीमा पर्याप्त खानेपानीको पहुँच पुगेको देखिन्छ भनेसबैभन्दा बढि दलित समूदायमा सबैले १०० प्रतिशत वा बाह्रै महिना पानी उपभोग गर्न सक्ने देखिन्छ भने ब्राह्मण समूदायका ४० प्रतिशत घरधुरीले मात्र बाह्रै महिना खानेपानी उपभोग गर्न सक्ने देखिन्छ । खानेपानी शुद्धिकरणको ज्ञानको दर ४५ प्रतिशत रहेको छ भने उच्चतम ज्ञानको दर ब्राह्मण समूदायमा८० प्रतिशत देखिन्छ , सबैभन्दा कम दलित समूदायमा १४.२८ प्रतिशत रहेको छ भने क्षेत्री र जनजातीमाक्रमशः ४६.१५ र ४५.७२ प्रतिशत रहेको छ । त्यसैगरी खानेपानी शुद्धिकरण गर्न अवलम्वन गर्ने विधि अन्र्तगत उमालेर प्रयोग गर्ने प्रयोगकर्ताको दर ६० प्रतिशत छ , शुद्धिकरणका कुनै विधि नै प्रयोग नगरी खानेपानी प्रयोग गर्ने प्रयोगकर्ताको दर १० प्रतिशत रहेको छ । त्यसमा दलित, ब्राहमण, क्षेत्री तथा जनजातीको पानी शुद्धिकरणको प्रयोग दर क्रमशः १००, १००, १०० र ८३ प्रतिशत रहेको छ ।
american_english: Water is an extremely important substance for living beings existing on this earth. Among them, humankind falls under the supreme creatures on earth. Therefore, drinking water is considered extremely important for humanity, so because the absence of suitable drinking water impedes even human growth and development, a study was conducted on the drinking water situation in Bamrang, Ward No. 3 of Diktel Rupakot Majhuwagadhi Municipality in Khotang District, in order to represent the overall geography and observe the condition of drinking water adequacy across various parts of Nepal. For this research article, a total of 120 households were selected for the sample in the community of Bamrang, Ward No. 3 of Diktel Rupakot Majhuwagadhi Municipality, Khotang District, using the lottery method from among probability sampling methods under quantitative and qualitative research methods. Among them, selecting 8 Brahmin households, 26 Chhetri households, 70 Janajati households, and 14 Dalit households, gathering data by having the necessary questionnaire filled out, collecting data from primary sources along with using secondary sources for other necessary data, and conducting the research by taking a total of 120 individuals as a sample from the members of 120 households, a survey conducted in the month of Falgun 2078 BS found that 51.67 percent of households use tap water, 43.33 percent of households use piped water, 3.33 percent use well water, and 1.67 percent use stream water for drinking, and drinking water usage through pipes was found to be highest in the Dalit community at 71.42 percent, while access to pipes was found to be lowest in the Brahmin community at only 20 percent. Overall, only 33.33 percent of households have access to water at home. It is highest in the Brahmin and Janajati communities at 40 percent each, and lowest in the Dalit community at 14.28 percent. Access to "one house, one tap" is seen in 31.67 percent of households, with the highest proportion in the Brahmin community where 80 percent of households have a tap, and the lowest in the Dalit community where 14.28 percent of households have a tap. Looking at the adequacy of drinking water, 85 percent of households appear to have reached adequate drinking water access, with the highest in the Dalit community where 100 percent can consume water across all twelve months of the year, whereas only 40 percent of households in the Brahmin community can consume drinking water all twelve months. The rate of knowledge regarding drinking water purification is 45 percent, while the highest rate of knowledge is seen in the Brahmin community at 80 percent, the lowest is in the Dalit community at 14.28 percent, and in the Chhetri and Janajati communities it is 46.15 and 45.72 percent, respectively. Likewise, under the methods adopted to purify drinking water, the user rate of boiling before use is 60 percent, while the user rate of consuming drinking water without applying any purification method at all is 10 percent. Among them, the water purification adoption rates of Dalit, Brahmin, Chhetri, and Janajati are 100, 100, 100, and 83 percent, respectively.

informal_english: Water is a proper vital thing for all living creatures on this earth. Out of all of them, humans are reckoned the top creatures on earth. Because of that, drinking water is seen as proper essential for people, and since going without decent water even gets in the way of human growth and development, this study looked into the water situation in Bamrang, Ward No. 3 of Diktel Rupakot Majhuwagadhi Municipality in Khotang District to give a fair picture of how drinking water stacks up across different parts of Nepal. For this research paper, a total of 120 households were picked for the sample in the community of Bamrang, Ward No. 3 of Diktel Rupakot Majhuwagadhi Municipality, Khotang District, using a lottery draw under probability sampling alongside quantitative and qualitative research methods. Out of that lot, 8 Brahmin households, 26 Chhetri households, 70 Janajati households, and 14 Dalit households were picked, sorting out data with questionnaires from primary sources and tapping into secondary sources for extra figures; sampling 120 folk across the 120 households in a survey from Falgun 2078 BS, it turned out that 51.67 per cent of households use tap water, 43.33 per cent use piped water, 3.33 per cent use well water, and 1.67 per cent use stream water for drinking, with piped water usage being highest in the Dalit community at 71.42 per cent and lowest in the Brahmin community at just 20 per cent. Overall, only 33.33 per cent of households actually have water right at home. It sits highest in the Brahmin and Janajati communities at 40 per cent each, and lowest in the Dalit community at 14.28 per cent. The "one house, one tap" setup is seen in 31.67 per cent of households, peaking in the Brahmin community where 80 per cent of homes have a tap, and dropping lowest in the Dalit community where only 14.28 per cent of homes have one. Looking at drinking water adequacy, 85 per cent of households seem to have enough water, with the Dalit community coming out on top where 100 per cent can use water all twelve months of the year, whereas only 40 per cent of households in the Brahmin community can get drinking water all twelve months. Knowing how to purify drinking water sits at 45 per cent overall, with the highest awareness in the Brahmin community at 80 per cent, the lowest in the Dalit community at 14.28 per cent, and Chhetri and Janajati groups at 46.15 and 45.72 per cent, respectively. What's more, for the methods used to clean drinking water, the rate of folk boiling it before use is 60 per cent, while 10 per cent drink their water without bothering with any purification method at all. In that regard, the water purification adoption rates for Dalit, Brahmin, Chhetri, and Janajati come in at 100, 100, 100, and 83 per cent, respectively.
